Lauren —

Quick answers below (high-level; I can join the sync for technical detail):

1) EU residency / Hosted API: We have two EU-hosted clusters (eu-west & eu-central) that support data processing and persistent storage within the EU. By default, requests that originate in EU regions are routed to EU clusters; we do not route EU customer data through US regions unless explicit cross-region routing is enabled by the customer. We can provide an architecture note for the security review.

2) Hybrid model: Supported. Common pattern: Hosted EU for customer-facing traffic + Dedicated or Private VPC in APAC for regulated workloads. We support policy-based routing at the request layer (route by region/header or customer tag) and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in alternate regions when capacity constraints occur — but fallback is opt-in for residency-sensitive traffic.

3) Private VPC / on-prem lead time: For an enterprise pilot (VPC with private control plane), typical lead time is ~6-8 weeks for standard cloud regions (APAC regions may be on the longer end due to network provisioning and compliance checks). On-prem packages vary a lot; early engagements start with an architecture workshop (1-2 weeks), then a 8-12 week integration depending on customer infra. We can fast-track an initial sandbox in 3-4 weeks in some cases.

Next steps I recommend before the sync: 
- Share a short tech note describing EU-hosted cluster residency guarantees (I’ll draft and attach).
- Decide if FinBank wants fallback disabled for residency-sensitive endpoints.
- Confirm attendees for the sync (infra/security + product).

I’ll join the call next week.

— Aditya
